semantic_contract: The function appends or prepends one record to a dynamically growing list owned by the receiver. The record is 16 bytes: three floats copied verbatim from the caller's triple, plus a fourth dword that is exactly 0 or 1 according to whether the caller asked for the front. That flag is not merely a direction selector - it is written into the record itself, so every record in the list permanently remembers the end it was inserted from. The list is reached at receiver+0xF0 and is an EASTL vector whose growth policy doubles the element count with a minimum of one, allocating through Spore's "Simulator" tag. The append path has an inlined fast case: it compares the insert cursor against the end cursor as UNSIGNED values, so a full list is detected as cursor-at-or-past-end rather than equality, and an empty list therefore takes the slow path. In the fast case the cursor is advanced by exactly 0x10 bytes before the payload is written, and if the cursor was null the function returns having advanced the cursor but written nothing. The prepend path always goes through the container's own insert helper, passing the head cursor as the insertion position, and the grow path always goes through the general insert helper, passing the end cursor. All three paths release the 16-byte stack frame and return void with the callee popping both arguments. Order is preserved: prepends go to the front, appends to the back, and the function never shrinks, reorders or reads the element count. Eleven of the fourteen observed callers sit in a single 0x00C13A30-0x00C2A699 code cluster, which is consistent with one class's methods being emitted together, and every caller discards the void result.
classification_rationale: The body is complete and every mechanism is read from the binary: all 44 instructions, the __thiscall ABI with two callee-cleaned stack arguments, the 0xF0 member offset with its ADD instruction, all three container cursor offsets, the 0x10 element stride with the LEA that establishes it, the unsigned full-test, the cursor-before-write ordering, the null-cursor quirk, the tag normalisation, the three exits, and the absence of globals and virtual dispatch. The container's implementation family is established from a string literal inside the shipped binary (the EASTL allocator.h path and the "Simulator" tag), and both insert helpers' bodies were read in full, including the growth policy. What is bounded, and named as the bound, is the OWNING CLASS and the element's field semantics: no SDK header declares a vector at +0xF0 alongside a flag at +0x19C and a container at +0x3E4, and the payload is only known to be three floats plus a dword. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld because the owning type is a material element and it is not established; STRUCTURAL_ONLY is too weak because the growth policy, the branch polarities and the inlined-versus-helper split are all established.
semantic_findings: The complete contract is 'insert {x, y, z, front ? 1 : 0} at the front or the back of the receiver's +0xF0 list'. Void, no globals, no virtual dispatch, no error path.

The direction flag is persisted in the record, not just consumed as a selector. SETNZ DL at 0x00c446ed produces exactly 0 or 1 and the same EDX is stored into element+0x0C on the append path, so the tag is a normalised boolean rather than the caller's raw byte.

Any non-zero direction byte selects the front, because both branches test the same AL and the second TEST at 0x00c4470b reuses the byte loaded at 0x00c446e5, unmodified by the SETNZ (which writes DL, not AL).
The element is 0x10 bytes, proven by the cursor arithmetic LEA ESI,[EAX+0x10] at 0x00c4472a and independently by the callee's growth arithmetic (count>>4 and capacity<<4).

Fullness is an UNSIGNED comparison, JNC at 0x00c44727, so the container is treated as full when cursor >= end. This makes an empty container full, which routes the first append through the grow helper. A signed or equality test would behave differently on a corrupt container and would not have produced this code.

The container is an EASTL vector, established from a string literal in the binary: the allocation at 0x00c43cc0 passes "Simulator" and "...EASTL\include\EASTL/allocator.h". The observed {first, cursor, end, +0x10 sentinel} layout and the max(1, 2*count) growth are EASTL's, not MSVC std::vector's.

The append path is inlined and the prepend and grow paths are not. That asymmetry is a deliberate optimisation of the common case and is reproduced exactly; the two helpers are private to this one container, with only three callers between them.

The cursor is advanced BEFORE the payload is stored, and a null cursor leaves the advanced value behind while writing nothing. Both behaviours are faithful to the binary and are preserved rather than corrected, because a reconstruction that tidied them would no longer match the original.

The grow path passes the END cursor as the insertion position, not the insert cursor. The two are equal whenever the branch is taken, so the difference is invisible in the current state space but is recorded because it constrains what the callee's position argument means.

The prepend path passes the container's +0x00 head cursor as the insertion position, and the callee's fast path requires pos == insert cursor, which is false for a non-empty list, so prepends on a non-empty list always take the callee's general insert and shift the whole buffer.

The callee 0x00c43f20 returns an iterator (mpFirst + index*0x10) that this function discards. Since this function is the only caller that ignores it, the iterator exists for other callers in the same private pair, not for this one.

Eleven of the fourteen callers lie in one contiguous 0x00C13A30-0x00C2A699 code region, and the sibling 0x00c44760 four bytes past this body touches the same receiver at +0x19C, -0xD4 and +0x3E4. Together these bound the owner at 0x3EC bytes or more and place its methods in one compilation unit.

Caller 0x00b34380 writes the dword 3 to receiver+0x1F0 immediately after a prepend, which suggests a state enum that is updated as a side effect of list maintenance; the connection is observed but its meaning is not established.
unresolved_questions: What class owns the vector at +0xF0? A recursive grep of the ModAPI tree for 0xF0, 0x3E4, 0x19C and 0x1F0 found no header declaring this combination. The owner is an opaque type carrying only the observed offsets. This is the material bound on the record.

What do the three floats mean, and what does the tag dword mean? Three consecutive floats and a normalised boolean are observed. Spore/SubSystem/PlanetModel.h's `{Vector3 mCenter; bool mCityZone; bool mVisible;}` is a shape-compatible candidate that would make the 0x10-byte element's last dword two bools, but PlanetModel.h declares no 0xF0 member and nothing observed links the two files, so no claim is made.

Why is the tag dword stored in the element when it is also the direction selector? Either the list is later partitioned by insertion end, or the two callers happen to want the same information. No static evidence distinguishes these.

Is the null-cursor advance a latent bug in the original? The function leaves receiver+0xF4 set to 0x10 when the cursor was null, so a subsequent call would write to address 0x10. Either the null case is unreachable in practice, or the original tolerates the corruption. Static evidence cannot decide, and the behaviour is preserved rather than defended against.

What do the other containers on the same receiver do? Sibling 0x00c44760 manipulates +0x3E4, -0xD4 and the flag at +0x19C, but its body was not read by this batch, so no relationship between the two containers is claimed.

body_reconstruction.claim_scope: The complete 44-instruction body is reconstructed with the same order of operations, the same member offset, the same container cursor offsets, the same element stride, the same tag normalisation, the same branch polarity, the same cursor-before-write ordering, the same null-cursor quirk, the same inlined-versus-helper split and the same three exits. preserved_semantics: the payload is read into registers before the branch, so it is identical on all three paths
the tag dword is exactly 0 or 1, never the caller's raw byte, and any non-zero direction byte means front
the tag is written into the element on the append path as well as selecting the prepend path
fullness is tested unsigned, so cursor >= end is the full condition and an empty container routes to the grow helper
the insert cursor is advanced by 0x10 before the payload is written
a null cursor leaves the advanced cursor in place and writes nothing
the prepend path passes the +0x00 head cursor as the position; the grow path passes the +0x08 end cursor
the callee pops both stack arguments (RET 0x8) and the 16-byte frame is released on every exit
the callees' return values, including the iterator 0x00c43f20 computes, are discarded
